prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

Title, set largest at the top left of the page: bookmilld
Deck beneath it: The mill's night porter — a small ever-running lodge that holds the dashboard's place on the shared rail, answers for its health, and points the way to the other daemons.

Hero: a modest gatehouse lodge at dusk, drawn warmly lit from within, standing beside a long covered footbridge — the shared rail — that runs across the upper half of the page connecting several small lodges on the horizon, each with its own lantern; the near neighbours carry small signs reading plated and arbiterd. The bookmilld lodge's own hanging sign reads bookmilld, and its front window shows a single tidy notice pinned inside: Bookmill Dashboard — pipeline status and controls will appear here. A note at the window: the front page keeps the dashboard's seat warm; the working dashboard still travels with the pipeline itself.

At the lodge door, a small brass speaking-tube with a card beside it reading status: ok, captioned — the heartbeat: anyone may knock and hear that all is well. Above the footbridge, a slender signboard of route markers, captioned: the shared navigation is served from one card of daemons, so every lodge shows the way to the others.

Two quiet details along the bottom:
- lower left: the lodge's night porter turning a lamp down gently, with two small hourglasses on the sill, captioned — told to close, it finishes serving whoever is inside, ten seconds' grace, then sleeps;
- lower right: a small workshop note pinned to the doorframe showing a hammer and a fresh timber beam, captioned — after a rebuild the lodge is torn down and re-founded, never merely nudged awake.

One warm accent colour belongs to the lit windows and lanterns along the rail; the lodges, bridge, and dusk stay in ink and grey wash.
